title: Chicken and Dumplings
subtitle: Post-shift hug in a pot
description: Post-shift hug in a pot. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Sear aromatics
steps.instruction: Brown meat in batches; remove. Sweat onion, carrot, celery in the same pot 8 minutes until edges soften.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.instruction: Return chicken to the pot with broth and vegetables. Simmer 35 minutes until chicken is tender; shred meat and return to the pot.

steps.title: Drop the dumplings
steps.instruction: Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt. Cut in butter, then stir in milk and eggs until a thick batter forms. Drop spoonfuls onto simmering broth, cover, and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid.

steps.title: Ladle and garnish
steps.instruction: Dumplings should be puffed and cooked through — a skewer should come out clean. Stir in parsley and serve hot from the pot.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up Chicken and Dumplings on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Post-shift hug in a pot. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
